primarySources.supports: Connector availability differs from Power Query availability. Direct browser DOM inspection found two Office 2016 columns and two Office 2019 columns with empty PDF cells, then two Microsoft 365 columns with PDF marked Included. Mac's source table does not list PDF. Web PDF entries concern SharePoint/OneDrive for work or school.
primarySources.limitation: Historical/stale matrix: no separate 2021 or 2024 columns, and not a definitive current inventory of every retail/LTSC SKU/build. An Applies To label is not connector-support evidence. Web entries do not establish a native Mac connector or a universal browser workflow.

primarySources.supports: Power Query Editor generally available to Microsoft 365 subscribers on Mac version 16.69 (23010700) or later; documented import sources exclude PDF.
primarySources.limitation: The version condition is for Editor availability, not native PDF support. Updating Mac Excel is not a documented way to reveal From PDF.

primarySources.supports: Windows path Data > Get Data > From File > From PDF; the Excel PDF section associates an additional-components message with .NET Framework 4.5 or higher. Text/CSV import can apply automatic data-type detection.
primarySources.limitation: The component message is an import/runtime-error branch, not proof that .NET restores a missing connector menu. Cross-check the newer connector page's Prerequisites: None wording; do not prescribe an obsolete installer indiscriminately.

primarySources.supports: Cross-product PDF connector documentation says Prerequisites: None and discusses bounded page extraction, multiline-row cleanup and MultiPageTables behavior.
primarySources.limitation: Does not itself establish connector availability in every Excel edition or Mac build. Its prerequisite wording is not fully aligned with the Excel-specific additional-components guidance.

primarySources.supports: Pdf.Tables and options including StartPage, EndPage and MultiPageTables. Result is a navigation-style table containing nested extracted tables, not automatically one cleaned worksheet.
primarySources.limitation: An M API reference is not a Mac compatibility workaround. The optional sample is documentation-based and not runtime-tested; displayed M Windows paths use single backslashes, with escaping only in this JSON representation.

primarySources.supports: Identify the installed Office product and version/build before making an edition-support diagnosis or support handoff.

primarySources.limitation: Updating is maintenance, not proof that an unsupported or undocumented connector becomes available.

sourceReconciliation.windowsMatrix: Direct browser inspection verified these six column groups: Office 2016 Home & Student/Home & Business/Standard/Professional; Office 2016 Professional Plus Standalone; Office 2019 Home & Student/Home & Business/Standard/Professional; Office 2019 Professional Plus Standalone; Microsoft 365 Home/Personal/Business/Business Premium; Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise. The PDF row is unmarked in the first four and Included in the last two. The matrix does not provide separate 2021/2024/LTSC columns. An earlier ledger-writing mistake calling all four older columns Office 2016 was corrected against this direct observation.
sourceReconciliation.macEditorVersusConnector: Mac version 16.69 establishes documented Power Query Editor availability, not a native PDF import/refresh connector. Neither an update, COM add-in nor Pdf.Tables code establishes missing Mac support.
sourceReconciliation.webVersusDesktop: PDF entries through SharePoint/OneDrive for work or school in the web matrix are a different environment. Do not promise universal browser availability, direct local-file import or Mac desktop refresh from those entries.
sourceReconciliation.componentDocumentationDiscrepancy: The Excel-specific import page names .NET Framework 4.5 or higher for an additional-components error; the newer cross-product PDF connector page says Prerequisites: None. Disclose both scopes. For that exact Windows error, check the current supported Excel/Windows configuration with official guidance or IT rather than automatically installing an obsolete framework. Neither statement proves the cause of a missing menu.
sourceReconciliation.loadedValuesVersusRefresh: Opening a workbook containing values extracted on supported Windows Excel is different from being able to refresh its PDF query on Mac.
sourceReconciliation.unsupportedFixes: No registry edits, random COM add-ins, blanket reinstall instructions, licence/sign-in cause claims or universal M-code workarounds without applicable evidence.

decisionGuide.symptom: The entire Get Data experience or Data tab appears absent
decisionGuide.nextAction: Identify desktop versus web, OS, product and build. Check ribbon visibility/customization using the appropriate platform guidance before narrowing the problem to PDF.
decisionGuide.boundary: A hidden ribbon and an unavailable connector are different conditions; do not assume either from the missing label alone.

decisionGuide.symptom: Get Data exists but From PDF is absent
decisionGuide.nextAction: Use the platform/edition branch and the documented matrix limits. Give Mac readers a clear stopping point and offer source CSV/XLSX or an approved extraction workflow rather than repeated reinstalls. For an unresolved Windows SKU/build, collect exact product details for support.
decisionGuide.boundary: The displayed Office 2019 columns were inspected, but do not extrapolate 2021/2024/LTSC support from them or a general Applies To label. A loaded workbook on Mac does not prove PDF-query refresh support.

decisionGuide.symptom: From PDF opens and then asks for additional components
decisionGuide.nextAction: Record the exact error and Windows/Excel version. Explain the Excel-specific .NET Framework note alongside the newer connector page's conflicting prerequisite wording, and use current official/administrator guidance for the supported configuration.
decisionGuide.boundary: This is a runtime/import-error branch, not a missing-menu repair. No indiscriminate legacy installer recommendation.

decisionGuide.symptom: Import opens but tables are empty, split, multiline or otherwise wrong
decisionGuide.nextAction: Distinguish PDF structure from a scanned-image/OCR problem. Inspect available tables, use bounded pages when appropriate, consider MultiPageTables behavior, and validate identifiers, dates, totals and row alignment against the source.
decisionGuide.boundary: OCR, Word conversion and table extraction do not guarantee exact layout or values. Prefer source CSV/XLSX; obtain approval before sending confidential material to any converter.

syntheticCsv.intendedLesson: Preserve InvoiceID as Text before destructive automatic conversion. Dates explicitly use day/month/year: the first is 3 October 2026, not March 10.
